sources.offline: pyproject.toml, package.json, package-lock.json, vendor/manifest.json, kit hash records, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, upstreams/registry.yaml, research/landscape.json, published Markdown

limits: A clean report is not proof of safety: advisory databases (OSV, the npm registry) only know what has been reported.
Licences come from licence files and registry metadata (GitHub, PyPI, npm), matched by keyword; they are not a legal review.
Link checks see status codes and redirects, not content: a parked or replaced page that answers 200 passes. Domain expiry is not checked.
GitHub links are checked at repository level; a missing file or anchor inside a live repository is not seen.
Python versions are checked at the newest release and the lowest release our range allows, not at every version in between.

Transitive Python dependencies are checked at the versions deps.dev resolves for our newest direct releases; an existing environment may hold other versions, and --installed checks only the installed versions of our direct dependencies.

Libraries bundled inside a vendored file (DOMPurify and KaTeX inside mermaid.min.js) are checked at the versions its receipt records; whether the bundling library reaches the affected code is not assessed.
Repository settings (secret scanning, Dependabot) are read only with an admin token; the weekly workflow cannot see them.
Offline mode checks only what the checkout shows (pins, hashes, licence files, lockfile, link schemes, install advice).

findings.subject: webkit:mermaid
findings.title: dompurify 3.4.12, bundled inside a vendored file, has 5 known advisories
findings.evidence: GHSA-cg2g-xh64-v4q7 (critical, fixed in 3.4.17): DOMPurify SAFE_FOR_TEMPLATES bypass: split template expressions survive in attached shadow root content on DOM output modes; GHSA-mrv2-3pqr-j5jr (high, fixed in 3.4.17): DOMPurify IN_PLACE: hook that removes a parent or sibling leaves the detached subtree's event handlers armed (incomplete fix for GHSA-p98j-92pf-mc4p); GHSA-55q2-fjhq-7xh7 (medium, fixed in 3.4.13): DOMPurify: IN_PLACE hook removal leaves a detached subtree executable, causing XSS; GHSA-6688-9rhm-gjv2 (low, fixed in 3.4.16): DOMPurify: IN_PLACE returns a force-removed rawtext root whose text carries attacker markup — pure HTML reparse executes; GHSA-c6gr-qvv4-5v3f (low, fixed in 3.4.17): DOMPurify: SMIL attributeName=href guard is skipped when PARSER_MEDIA_TYPE is application/xhtml+xml
findings.action: dompurify comes inside another library's file: take the first release of that library that bundles dompurify >=3.4.17, and say in the receipt whether the affected code is reachable.

findings.subject: npm:fsevents
findings.title: fsevents runs an install script (only on darwin)
findings.action: Read the script; in CI prefer npm ci --ignore-scripts where the package works without it.
findings.accepted: Optional, macOS-only dependency of Playwright (os: darwin), so CI and Linux machines never install it. Read on 2026-11-01 (#151): the registry's manifest for 2.3.2 lists install "node-gyp rebuild" (gypfile), but the tarball the lockfile pins (its sha512 matches) has no binding.gyp and its package.json has no install script; it ships a prebuilt fsevents.node, so npm runs nothing at install. Re-read it when Playwright moves to another fsevents. (2026-11-01)

findings.subject: url:https://github.com/google/feabench
findings.title: google/feabench is archived (read-only, no fixes)
findings.action: Show it as "unmaintained" (status or note) instead of removing it; plan a replacement if we use its code.
findings.accepted: Shown as archived where we name it: its catalogue card (research/landscape.json notes) and research/agent-toolkits-2026-10.md. Prior art only (it needs COMSOL); we use none of its code. (2026-11-01)
